SMTO-SKL-0167 — GitHub sent back something SMTO couldn't use

GUID: 5c83e401-066d-50f1-a188-1b252278f73c
Slug: github-provider-response-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO got an answer from GitHub, but it was damaged, not what SMTO expected, or pointed to a download location SMTO doesn't trust. SMTO didn't use it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you asked for a change, open the issue, pull request or release on github.com and check whether the change is there before asking again. This error does not establish whether a change you asked for reached GitHub, so check before repeating it.
  2. Ask SMTO to look up the same thing again. A damaged or unexpected reply is often a one-off, and a new lookup gets a fresh answer.
  3. If it fails the same way again for the same item, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. A repeat failure on one item points to a problem SMTO's developers need to see.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the information you asked for, or you can see on github.com that your change is in place.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat a change on GitHub until you've confirmed it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The GitHub response failed validation: an unparseable or non-object JSON body, a list page larger than requested, an unexpected result shape, or a download redirect to a non-GitHub location.

What this means

  • Transfer URL, JSON parsing, result type, bounded collection or service projection checks reject the returned provider data. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Transfer URL, JSON parsing, result type, bounded collection or service projection checks reject the returned provider data.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact shape, bound or destination validation failure and operation receipt.

How to fix it

  • Raised by GitHubClient.read_json/request (invalid JSON or non-dict/list result), transfer_url (redirect outside GitHub's signed download hosts), GitHubService.page (non-list or oversized page) or service projection errors before any write dispatch; writes that fail this way after dispatch are reported as an unknown outcome instead. Repeat a read to inspect current provider state, and never assume a write failed safely.
  • Inspect provider status using a new read. The response was malformed or did not match the bounded contract; never assume a write failed safely.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported provider data validates before use; post-dispatch writes retain their unknown-outcome handling.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
